source.title: NVIDIA HGX Platform specifications
source.notes: HGX values are for 8 GPUs. FP4 lists sparse and dense explicitly. Other Tensor Core values are sparse and NVIDIA states dense is one half of the shown value. Values below are derived per-GPU dense peaks. hbm_bandwidth_gb_per_s is the per-GPU HBM peak bandwidth and is the MBU denominator; B200 and B300 both publish 8 TB/s.

mixed_input_rules.notes: dense_tflops_per_gpu is keyed by a single dtype, so resolve_peak() only auto-resolves a GEMM whose tensor inputs share one dtype. A GEMM with operands of different widths needs an explicit mfu_peak_tflops in its semantic rule. Rule: on Blackwell the tcgen05 mxf8f6f4 instruction path runs fp8/fp6/fp4 operands at one rate, so a mixed-input GEMM runs at the rate of its *widest* operand -- the slower rate -- not at the narrow operand's headline rate.

fp8_x_mxfp4.note: fp8 activations x mxfp4 weights (e.g. SGLang MegaMoE grouped GEMM on B200) run at the fp8 dense peak 4500 TFLOPS/GPU, not the fp4 peak 9000. Verified against a GLM5.2 prefill capture.
fp8_x_mxfp4.mbu: leave empty when the narrow operand is sub-byte and the kernel fuses multiple GEMMs: a single (M,N,K) cannot express its HBM traffic. Declare storage_dtypes.b as an explicit unmodeled marker, e.g. "mxfp4-subbyte-unmodeled".

mixed_input_rules.unlisted_combinations: Apply the same widest-operand rule, and record in the evidence why the chosen peak_dtype_key is the throughput-limiting operand.
